_about: Plant care tasks for USDA zone 6 (Kansas City area). Dates are typical windows; 'trigger' lets the daily weather run move the start date. Trigger types: soil_ge / soil_le (7-day soil average at 2.5in, °F), last_frost (day after the last spring frost once 7+ frost-free days are in view), first_frost / hard_freeze (fall lows ≤32°F / ≤28°F; offset in days, negative = before).

tasks.note: Classic cue: prune when forsythia blooms. Cut out dead/crossing canes; shape to 12–18" (Knock Outs can go to ~1/3 height).
Feed after new growth starts; repeat every 6 weeks through early August if you want max blooms.
No fertilizer after mid-August so growth hardens off before frost. Deadhead as needed.

tasks.task: Mound mulch over the base for winter
tasks.note: After the first hard freeze, mound 8–10" of mulch or compost over the crown. Don't prune now.
Wait until buds leaf out so you can see what's dead. Do NOT cut back healthy stems: that removes this year's flowers. (Endless Summer types are forgiving.)

tasks.task: Deadhead / light shaping right after flowering
tasks.note: Only window for shaping. No pruning after early August; next year's buds form in late summer.

tasks.task: Mulch the base; leave stems standing
tasks.note: 2–3" of mulch over the root zone protects the flower buds on the stems.
Blooms on new wood. Panicle: cut by about 1/3 to a strong framework. Smooth (Annabelle): cut to 12–18" (taller if stems flop).

plants.name: Spring-flowering shrubs (lilac, forsythia, azalea, viburnum, spring spirea)

tasks.note: They set next year's flowers by midsummer, so prune within ~3 weeks of blooms fading. Remove the oldest 1/3 of stems at the base to renew.

tasks.task: Shear after the spring growth flush
tasks.note: Keep the bottom wider than the top so it stays full. Boxwood: thin a few interior branches for airflow.
Light touch-up only. Pruning later pushes tender growth that winter burns.
Before new green shoots get tall. Tie big clumps with twine first for easy cleanup. Divide every 3–4 years in spring.

plants.name: Perennials (hosta, daylily, coneflower, salvia, black-eyed Susan)

tasks.note: Cut last year's stems to the ground and divide overgrown clumps as shoots emerge. Top-dress with compost.

tasks.task: Fall cutback (leave seedheads for birds if you like)
tasks.note: After a hard freeze blackens foliage. Hostas and daylilies get cut to the ground; coneflower/black-eyed Susan can stand for birds and winter interest.

tasks.task: Pinch back tips (repeat every 2–3 weeks until July 4)
tasks.note: Pinch off the top 1" of each stem when it reaches 6". Stop by July 4 or you'll lose fall flowers.
Remove dead, crossing and low branches while dormant. OAKS: never prune April–July (oak wilt). Leave big limbs to an arborist.
Trees planted in the last 3 years: 10 gal per inch of trunk diameter every 2 weeks if it's dry, until the ground freezes.
Open the center, remove water sprouts and crossing limbs. Peaches: prune last (late March is fine).
On a calm day above 40°F with no freeze for 24 hrs. Smothers overwintering scale, mites and aphid eggs.
They leaf out late here. Cut back only to live wood (scratch-test for green). Don't top them ('crape murder').
Trim only the new growth. Most conifers won't regrow from bare old wood. Pines: pinch new 'candles' by half.
Wait until leaves yellow (about 6 weeks after bloom); they recharge next year's bulb.
Once soil cools below ~60°F, before the ground freezes. Plant 3× as deep as the bulb is tall.

tasks.task: Plant cool-season crops (peas, lettuce, spinach, onions)
tasks.note: Soil 45°F+ and workable (not soggy). Light frosts are fine for these.
After the last frost with nights staying above 50°F. Harden off transplants for a week first.
Pull spent plants (toss diseased tomato vines, don't compost), add compost or shredded leaves, mulch.

plants.name: Tender / container plants (tropicals, citrus, houseplants summering outside)

tasks.note: After the last frost with nights above 50°F. Start in shade for a week so leaves don't scorch.
Before nights drop below ~45–50°F for tropicals. Check for pests and hose off before bringing in.
